risks.note: The Board's Report states that out of the Company's total GWP, "Motor 59.9%", with Fire 9.7%, Engineering 2.0%, Health, Travel & Personal Accident 18.3% and other lines 10.1% — so a majority of the book, and its pricing, third-party liability and claims experience, sits in a single regulated line.

"The combined ratio of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 was 110.7% as against 109.3% for the previous financial year", i.e. claims plus expenses continued to exceed premium and the ratio deteriorated year-on-year, while the loss ratio was broadly flat at 72.9% versus 72.8%.
risks.risk: Underwriting result remains loss-making at the combined-ratio level and widened during the year

risks.note: "IRDAI requires insurance companies to maintain a minimum solvency of 1.5 times which is calculated in a manner as specified in the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024"; the Company stood at 2.42 times as at March 31, 2026 versus 2.24 times a year earlier, so premium growth is permanently tied to maintaining regulatory capital.
risks.risk: Regulatory solvency floor constrains growth and capital flexibility

risks.note: The Scheme is "conditional upon receipt of observation/no-objection letters from the Stock Exchanges", approval by the requisite majority of each class of creditors and members, votes in favour exceeding those against, "approvals from the Competition Commission of India and the IRDAI under the Insurance Act, 1938" and sanction by the NCLT — a multi-regulator chain with no stated completion date, and the Appointed Date is itself the Effective Date.
risks.risk: Execution and approval risk on the proposed amalgamation of the holding company

risks.note: "the trademarks and brand names 'DIGIT' and 'GO DIGIT', together with other related trademarks central to the Company's business and brand identity, were assigned by Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited ('the holding Company') to Go Digit Solutions Private Limited, a Promoter Group entity"; the earlier licence was terminated and a new licence executed, so the Company's core brand right is contractual and rests with a promoter-group party.
risks.risk: Brand is owned outside the Company and used under licence

risks.note: "The net retention ratio and the net earning ratio ... were 73.7% and 101.1% respectively as against 80.0% and 97.8% respectively for the previous financial year" — a lower retention ratio means a larger share of risk is ceded, making outcomes more dependent on reinsurer capacity, pricing and recoveries.
risks.risk: Reduced net retention increases dependence on reinsurance arrangements

risks.note: "The industry's Gross Direct Premium ('GDP') grew from ₹ 3,07,66,069 Lakhs in FY2024-25 to ₹ 3,36,12,268 Lakhs in FY2025-26, marking a growth of 9.3%" — the Company writes general insurance in India only, with market share of 3.4% versus 3.3%, so its top line moves with Indian non-life industry growth and share shifts.
risks.risk: Growth is tied to a single industry and geography whose own growth is cyclical

sk.overview: India's insurance distribution market is transforming from fragmented offline agent/broker/bancassurance channels toward tech-enabled 'phygital' brokers using the PoSP model. Rising incomes, digital adoption and IRDAI's 'Insurance for All by 2047' vision underpin growth, especially in B30+ (beyond top-30 city) markets. Industry data sourced from the commissioned Redseer Report (May 2026).
sk.structure: Life, health and motor account for ~92% of GDPI (FY2025). Distribution shifting from offline agents/brokers/bancassurance to tech-enabled digital brokers adopting the PoSP model. B30+ markets (rest of India ex top-30 cities) are 50-60% of premium and expected to grow up to 1.6x faster than T30.
